patches.before:
She looked at Hessa.

Hessa looked at me.

The woman said, “Why would I do a wall?”
patches.after:
She looked at Hessa.

Hessa kept her pencil on the ledger.

The woman said, “Why would I do a wall?”
patches.reason: Hessa does not need to trade a generic look with Greg. Keeping her physically attached to the measurement record preserves her procedural authority while leaving Rinna to answer for her own work.

patches.after:
Rusk marked another line on the cloth sheet.

“You owe him money.”
patches.reason: Rusk's answer lands more specifically when he keeps doing the work Greg interrupted. The debt explanation is casual because the work does not stop for it.

patches.before:
He looked confused by the question.

“You own it,” Arlo said.
patches.after:
Arlo looked down at the regulator.

“You own it.”
patches.reason: Arlo's confusion is about Greg inflating a simple object-ownership request into a larger role. Routing the beat through the regulator makes the answer more specifically Arlo and removes a generic facial summary.

patches.before: She nodded. No follow-up. I had expected one. Interesting. Then she asked Jorren, “You working gate tomorrow?”
patches.after: Nessa tucked the coins deeper into the laundry basket. No follow-up. I had expected one. Interesting. Then she asked Jorren, “You working gate tomorrow?”
patches.reason: Nessa's lack of curiosity becomes stronger when she simply finishes the transaction and moves to the next practical relationship thread. The basket carries the beat better than a generic nod.

patches.before:
Mara brought Jorren water without being asked.

He looked offended.

She said, “You work tomorrow.”

He drank it.
patches.after:
Mara brought Jorren water without being asked.

Jorren put two fingers around the cup but did not lift it.

She said, “You work tomorrow.”

He drank it.
patches.reason: Their familiarity is more legible through the cup itself: token resistance, her practical reason, then compliance. It reads like an existing routine rather than a narrated emotion.

patches.before:
“Why not mason now?”

She looked at me.

“Because the mill is stopped now.”
patches.after:
“Why not mason now?”

Etta set one wet hand on the gate.

“Because the mill is stopped now.”
patches.reason: Etta's answer is about the machine in front of her. Keeping her hand on the failed gate makes the priority physical and worksite-specific instead of explanatory.

patches.before:
Berren objected.

“No.”

Alden looked at him.

“It is injured.”
patches.after:
Berren objected.

“No.”

Alden pointed at Berren’s rebuilt boot.

“It is injured.”
patches.reason: Alden is running the spar and his rule is concrete. Pointing at the actual injury keeps him operational rather than turning the exchange into a face-off.

patches.after:
Berren shifted once on the rebuilt boot, opened his mouth, then closed it.

“Fine.”
patches.reason: His acceptance is stronger when the body that is forcing the decision is present in the beat. The pause remains, but it belongs to Berren's actual physical limit rather than an abstract change of mind.
